A second investigator, starting fresh with the same tools, tested the kind of each fault in your draft answer. Their findings:

### `ts-station-service`: you said `database_call_failed`. They conclude `network_partition` (confidence: medium).
Scope: Affected: ts-station-service's database access. From about 15:24 in the incident, every station call that needs a pooled MySQL connection (SELECT station, findByNames, findAll, queryForIdBatch, and the idlist and query Server spans on top of them) hangs for about 30 s and then fails, while the pod itself stays up and emits metrics and logs. Not affected: station's CPU and memory, and MySQL's service to other services (route, auth, user, train, order and travel DB calls all succeed in the incident). Station's DB calls succeeded only in the first minute of the window, before 15:24.
Ruled out:
- `database_call_failed`: The claimed kind is rejected as the cause. The errors are connection-level (Communications link failure with no packets received, HikariPool 'Connection is not available' after 30000 ms, 'No operations allowed after connection closed'), not SQL-layer throws. They hit every statement needing a connection, not particular statements while others succeed. The boundary rules put connection-level errors on the network.
- `database_call_slow`: The Client-side SELECT ts.station span stays at about 0.2 ms when it runs, and the Internal SELECT station spans succeed at about 0.4 ms in the first minute. The 30 s is spent waiting for a pooled connection before the statement is sent. Statement time is not growing, and the call count collapses from 856 to 5.
- `application_exception`: Station's error and warning logs are all pool and driver text (HikariPool, Communications link failure, SQLState 08S01/08003). No application-code exception is logged as the cause.
- `pod_unavailable`: Station is not gone. Its metric rows stay at 114.5 per minute against 140.2 normal, and its logs continue at 10.7 per minute. Its spans fall, but it is still answering requests, with errors.
- `container_cpu_saturated`: Station container CPU averages 0.01 in the incident against 0.04 normal, so the container is not CPU-bound.
- `container_memory_saturated`: Station container working set averages 587.2 MB against 571.4 MB normal, about +2.8%, well below any saturation signature, and memory limit utilisation is flat at 0.19.
Evidence:
- In the incident, the Internal SELECT station spans with status Error number 10 and take about 30001 ms (p50). The Client SELECT ts.station spans number 5 with p50 about 0.24 ms, against 856 normal. The Internal SELECT station spans with status Unset number 5 at about 0.42 ms, against 614 normal. Statement time is flat when it runs, and the drop in count is the calls that never get a connection.

The driver has not received any packets from the server', 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms', 'No operations allowed after connection closed', and SQLState 08S01 and 08003. No application exception is logged. Errors run from 15:24:04 to 15:28:49.

From about 15:24 in the incident, every station call that needs a pooled MySQL connection (SELECT station, findByNames, findAll, queryForIdBatch, and the idlist and query Server spans on top of them) hangs for about 30 s and then fails, while the pod itself stays up and emits metrics and logs. ruled_out.why: The claimed kind is rejected as the cause. The errors are connection-level (Communications link failure with no packets received, HikariPool 'Connection is not available' after 30000 ms, 'No operations allowed after connection closed'), not SQL-layer throws. They hit every statement needing a connection, not particular statements while others succeed. The boundary rules put connection-level errors on the network.

The Client-side SELECT ts.station span stays at about 0.2 ms when it runs, and the Internal SELECT station spans succeed at about 0.4 ms in the first minute. The 30 s is spent waiting for a pooled connection before the statement is sent. Statement time is not growing, and the call count collapses from 856 to 5.
Station's error and warning logs are all pool and driver text (HikariPool, Communications link failure, SQLState 08S01/08003). No application-code exception is logged as the cause.
Station is not gone. Its metric rows stay at 114.5 per minute against 140.2 normal, and its logs continue at 10.7 per minute. Its spans fall, but it is still answering requests, with errors.
Station container CPU averages 0.01 in the incident against 0.04 normal, so the container is not CPU-bound.
Station container working set averages 587.2 MB against 571.4 MB normal, about +2.8%, well below any saturation signature, and memory limit utilisation is flat at 0.19.

**Verdict: `database_call_failed` is not supported. The evidence points to a network partition on the station-to-MySQL connection (`network_partition`, same class as `network_loss`). Confidence is moderate.**

**What the lead's evidence shows, and what it misses**

- The 30 s errors are real. From 15:24 onward, every station `SELECT station` Internal span that fails takes about 30,001 ms, and the Server spans for `idlist` and `StationController.query` also time out at about 30 s.
- The lead's "DB call is slow" reading is incomplete. The Client-side `SELECT ts.station` span is 0.2 ms when it does run. But the Client DB span count fell from 856 normal to 5 abnormal. So most statements never reach the driver. The 30 s is spent waiting for a pooled connection, before the statement is sent.
- The lead's CPU and memory check is fine. Station memory is about 3% above normal and CPU is lower. The pod stays up, with metrics arriving at 114 rows/min against 140 normal.

**Why the failure is connection-level, not an SQL-layer throw**

- The logs carry driver and pool text, not a SQL error. The text is `Communications link failure ... The driver has not received any packets from the server`, `HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms`, and `No operations allowed after connection closed`. The 08S01 SQLState is a connection-state code, not a statement error.
- The failures hit every statement that needs a connection: `SELECT station`, `findByNames`, `findAll` and `queryForIdBatch`. Nothing is failing at once on particular statements while others succeed.
- Per the boundary rules, link failures, connection timeouts and "no connection available" point to the network, not to `database_call_failed`.

**Evidence against `database_call_failed`**

- The database is not the problem. Other services' MySQL calls in the incident (`ts-route`, `ts-auth`, `ts-user`, `ts-train`, `ts-order`, `ts-travel`) are fast with no errors, on the same MySQL instance.
- Station's own DB calls succeed only in the first minute of the window (5 calls at 0.2–0.5 ms, all before 15:24). From 15:24 onward, none succeed. That is a cut, not a statement-specific fault.

**Why the answer is network_partition and not loss**

- The station-side calls hang until the 30 s timeout while the MySQL server stays healthy for others. That is the partition shape: calls hang until a timeout, with both ends alive.
- Network loss and partition are the same equivalence class here, so either is scored correctly. I cannot separate them further.

**Caveats**

- No `hubble_*` per-connection metrics exist for this case, so I cannot confirm the station-to-MySQL pair directly.
- Hikari pool exhaustion from hung connections would look similar from station's side. The boundary rules still put connection-level errors on the network, so I am not treating the pool as a separate cause.
- The cause of the cut is outside this check. I did not test whether station is the right service to blame.
